business_problem: Benefit Street Partners needed to answer investment-committee follow-up questions faster, compare lender marks across shared loans, and review 300-page credit agreements for clauses that could shift value away from lenders without waiting on slow manual analysis or outside counsel to read every page.
solution_summary: Benefit Street Partners built two AI-assisted underwriting tools around Codex and GPT-6 Astra. For loan valuation work, portfolio manager Anant Kumar created a BDC mark tracker that pulls public SEC filings from business development companies and compares how different firms value the same loan, giving BSP a dashboard for benchmarking its own marks. Kumar used Codex to draft and review the application code, then iterate on features and interface changes in hours. For document analysis, BSP assembled memos from leading law firms on clauses and lender risks, then paired that reference material with uploaded 300-page credit agreements inside a credit agreement analyzer. After BSP refactored the tool with GPT-6 Astra and put it in a company-hosted portal, the system could ingest long agreements, synthesize a first-pass risk review, and hand the result to analysts for more than an hour of human validation before any investment decision.

solution_components.name: BDC mark tracker
solution_components.role: Compares how business development companies value the same loan so BSP can benchmark its own marks against other holders' valuations.

solution_components.name: Codex
solution_components.role: Helps Kumar draft, review, and refine the code behind BSP's internal underwriting tools.

solution_components.name: Credit agreement analyzer
solution_components.role: Processes uploaded credit agreements and surfaces clause-level issues and lender risks in a first-pass underwriting review.

solution_components.name: GPT-6 Astra
solution_components.role: Powers the refactored analyzer that ingests long agreements and synthesizes the initial review inside BSP's portal.

data_flow: Public SEC filings feed the BDC mark tracker so BSP can compare its loan marks with other holders' valuations. Separately, analysts upload long credit agreements and pair them with law-firm memos on risky clauses inside the credit agreement analyzer, where GPT-6 Astra produces a first-pass review in the company-hosted portal. Analysts then review the output before using it in underwriting rounds and investment-committee follow-ups.

business_outcome: Benefit Street Partners can now turn a round of investment-committee comments in a day, often answer follow-up questions during the meeting itself, build the first version of its BDC mark tracker in about a day, and generate a first-pass credit agreement analysis in about 20 minutes before human review, adding more review capacity and confidence within the same underwriting window.
